title: Theseus: The Black Sails
subtitle: Homecoming, a forgotten signal, and the sea gets a name

narrativeBlocks.title: Ariadne left behind
narrativeBlocks.body: Sailing home, Theseus puts in at Naxos — and leaves Ariadne there. The versions disagree wildly: she is abandoned, or forgotten, or claimed by the god Dionysus. Plutarch reports one telling where Theseus leaves her because he has fallen for another woman, Aegle.

narrativeBlocks.title: The forgotten sail
narrativeBlocks.body: Before he left Athens, Theseus promised Aegeus a signal: sail home under a white sail if his son lives; the crew returns under black sails if he has died. In the joy — or the shame — of the return, the sail is never changed.

narrativeBlocks.title: Aegeus on the cliff
narrativeBlocks.body: From the Acropolis, the old king watches the ship round the point under black sails. Believing his son dead, he throws himself from the rock — and the sea that takes his name is called the Aegean.

narrativeBlocks.title: King of Athens
narrativeBlocks.body: Theseus returns a hero and an orphan king in one stroke. The victory over the Minotaur ends the tribute; the cost of the forgotten sail makes him ruler of Athens.

narrativeBlocks.title: A flaw that defines him
narrativeBlocks.body: This is the Theseus pattern: brilliant in trials, careless in aftermaths. He will leave Ariadne, forget the sail, and later join Pirithous on reckless ventures — the hero whose homecomings cost more than his journeys.

quiz.explanation: Theseus promised a white sail for survival, black for death; the crew forgot to change it, and Aegeus threw himself from the rock — naming the Aegean Sea.

quiz.prompt: What did the white sail mean?

choices.text: That Theseus had survived — the crew was to swap the black sail for white on a successful return
That the ship carried no weapons

quiz.explanation: White sail = Theseus lives, black = dead. The crew forgot to change it and Aegeus, seeing black, threw himself from the rock.
